fixes.explanation: Priests do show up in this passage, but in verse 7, and they're reeling from strong drink there. Verse 5 doesn't name priests at all. Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts will be a crown "…to the remnant of His people…"

Yes, baker. Isaiah says "Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine." Priests and prophets are named right there in the verse. That's a heavy part of the passage, so I think it's worth slowing down on.

Soldiers aren't named in this verse. Isaiah says "Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine." The verse names priests and prophets, and I think that's why it lands so hard.

That's true. Isaiah says the priests and prophets are "…muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments." The strong drink has them muddled and stumbling. Verse 7 says this about priests and prophets together.

That's it. The text asks, "To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?" Those are the people it names, and they're the littlest ones around. It's asked as a question, so I'll leave the answer where the text leaves it.
Elders and city gates aren't in these questions. The verse asks, "To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?" It names the littlest ones, not the older, wiser ones.

No kings in these questions, friend. Verse 9 asks, "To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?" The questions point at babies, and that's about as far from a throne as you can get.

Yes, baker. Isaiah says "…with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people…" That's the way verse 11 gives. Verse 12 says these are the people to whom He has said, "This is the place of rest…"
Dreams aren't in this verse, friend. Isaiah says "…with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people…" That's the way verse 11 gives.
A voice from the clouds would be quite a scene, but Isaiah doesn't say it. He says "…with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people…" The verse names foreign tongues.
That's not how verse 12 ends, friend. He says, "This is the place of rest, let the weary rest…" and then the verse says "But they would not listen." So the people didn't listen to the offer.
Yes, false. After the offer of rest, the verse says "But they would not listen." The offer was on the table, and they would not listen. I think that's a quiet, sad little sentence.

The summit is where Ephraim's crown sits in verse 1, and verse 2 says that crown will be smashed to the ground. This verse doesn't send anybody climbing. Isaiah says they "…will go stumbling backward…"
